label: The neuron strongly activates on numeric tokens (e.g. years, percentages, counts, large numbers), so it’s detecting numbers/statistical values in the text.

The neuron is simply a “sentence-position” detector – it has its strongest activations on the first few real tokens of a sentence (e.g. the initial determiner or auxiliary) and then decays as you move further into the sentence.
The neuron flags unusually informative or low‐frequency “content” words (i.e. non‐function words that carry specific meaning).
The neuron is specifically responding to the start‐of‐sequence marker, i.e. it fires strongly on the “<bos>” token.
The neuron is triggered by numeric expressions and measurements (digits, quantities, and related numeric tokens).
